sections.content:
Population change in Windsor and Maidenhead in 2032

The population in Windsor and Maidenhead is projected to increase from 154,869 people in 2022 to 157,280 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net international migration, which will increase the population by 4,724 people.

This is different to the majority of areas in England, where net internal migration is projected to be the biggest factor in population change.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Windsor and Maidenhead
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Windsor and Maidenhead, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More deaths than births mean that the population is projected to decrease by 706, with 13,553 births and 14,259 deaths in Windsor and Maidenhead between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would decrease the population in Windsor and Maidenhead by 0.5%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is not projected to change the population substantially, with 107,572 people moving to the area and 107,600 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 1,495, with 2,935 people moving to the area and 4,430 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Windsor and Maidenhead by 1.0%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 4,724, with 17,323 people moving to the area and 12,599 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Windsor and Maidenhead by 3.1%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Windsor and Maidenhead in 2032

The median age in Windsor and Maidenhead is projected to rise from 42 years in 2022 to 45 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 21% of the population in Windsor and Maidenhead are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 18% in 2022.

sections.title: The 0 to 9 age group are set to see the largest change in Windsor and Maidenhead between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Windsor and Maidenhead is projected to stay the same, at around 63%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 280 to 311 over the same time period.

This is above average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Windsor and Maidenhead?

In 2032, 20% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 23% in 2022.

This is the same as the average for England in 2032.

Looking at the youngest age groups in Windsor and Maidenhead between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 5% to 4%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 10% to 9%
